analysis.title: Stellantis NV Deep dive: 2027 reset ahead; recovery only from 2028
key_insights: BofA reiterates Underperform on Stellantis and cuts its price objective to EUR 3.50 from EUR 5.50, against a EUR 3.83 share price. The cut is almost entirely a c.EUR 4bn lower industrial net cash forecast for 2027-28, worth about EUR 2 per share.

BofA forecasts 2027 adjusted operating income (AOI) of EUR 2.2bn, a 1.4% margin. Consensus is EUR 3.9bn and 2.4%. Shipments fall c.3% y/y, and material-cost inflation and competition absorb much of the planned value creation program (VCP) savings of about EUR 2.0bn.
BofA forecasts a 2027 industrial free cash flow outflow of EUR 2.7bn against consensus of EUR -300m. This would miss Stellantis' target of free cash flow breakeven.

Q3 2026 adjusted EBIT was EUR 256m versus Visible Alpha consensus of EUR 162m (0.7% margin). Industrial free cash flow was EUR -4.0bn and industrial net cash fell to EUR 5.4bn. BofA estimates a de facto industrial net debt of about EUR -5bn before the convertible proceeds and after adjusting for factoring.

Stellantis' reported Q3 AOI bridge differs materially from the bridge implied by subtracting H1 from 9M, though both show the same EUR 166m improvement. Vehicle net price is +EUR 23m reported versus an implied -EUR 228m, which reduces earnings visibility.

FY26 guidance was reaffirmed with net tariff costs cut to c.EUR 1.0bn from EUR 1.0-1.2bn. Management expects a large Q4 seasonal working-capital inflow and mid-hundreds of millions of VCP savings. It deferred detailed 2027 guidance to the FY results.

October US retail sales fell 9% y/y against market growth of c.3%. Jeep fell 14% and the smaller brands fell almost 50%. Days' supply was 99 versus 59 for the market, and incentives were c.$4,800 per vehicle, 37% above the industry average.

October European registrations for Stellantis including Leapmotor were flat to down 2% against market growth of c.3-5%. Legacy brands were likely down high single digits, offset by triple-digit Leapmotor growth. Chinese OEMs keep gaining share ahead of potential import restrictions.

BofA's Q4 2026 estimates are below consensus. It forecasts shipments down 5.6% y/y, with North America down c.15% against consensus of c.-7%. It sees further FY27 estimate cuts ahead of FY26 results in late February 2027.

2027 regional view: Europe AOI of EUR -625m versus consensus of c.EUR -180m, and North America AOI of EUR 960m, c.50% below consensus. The North American drag comes from no IEEPA tariff refund (EUR 400m in H1 26), possible Canadian import tariffs (EUR -400m) and raw-material inflation (about EUR -1bn).

Recovery begins in 2028. BofA forecasts group AOI of EUR 4.9bn (3.1% margin), with North American margin rising from 1.4% to c.4%. This is still below consensus and Stellantis' 5% target, and FCF of EUR 0.7bn compares with the company's EUR 3bn ambition.
BofA expects Stellantis to miss its 2030 targets: revenue of c.EUR 167bn versus the EUR 190bn ambition, AOI margin of 3.9% versus 7%, and industrial FCF of EUR 2.4bn versus EUR 6bn.

The EUR 7.6bn reported 2026E industrial net cash could be viewed as c.EUR 10bn of underlying industrial net debt after adjusting for hybrid bonds, leases, pensions and factoring. BofA forecasts industrial net cash bottoming at EUR 4.9bn in 2027.

Stellantis is rated BBB- with a negative outlook by S&P and Baa3 stable by Moody's, one notch above junk. BofA sees a meaningful risk of a cut to non-investment grade during 2027, which it estimates could add 50-100bp to new unsecured funding costs.

BofA says a capital raise is not its base case. With a market cap of only c.EUR 11.5bn, even a modest raise would be heavily dilutive, so the overhang could keep investors out until free cash flow turns positive.

Stellantis pays an estimated 5-6% on three- to seven-year debt, about 2 percentage points more than a year ago. The 10Y yield is c.6.6% versus c.3.9%. Annual industrial maturities are c.EUR 2-3bn through 2029.

The sum-of-the-parts valuation uses average 2027/28 estimates, with EV/sales of 0.14x, EV/EBIT of 3.3x and adjusted P/E of 3.9x. It now applies peer multiples to adjusted EPS, which excludes c.EUR 900m of special items, and yields EUR 3.50 per share.

The launch pipeline is thin in North America and Europe through 2027. Jeep Grand Cherokee, Wrangler and Gladiator facelifts and the Dodge Durango arrive only in H2 2027. Fleet age peaks at 7.8 years in 2028E, and the product cycle accelerates from 2028-29.

market_movers.rationale: PO cut from EUR 5.50 on a c.EUR 4bn lower 2027-28 industrial net cash forecast and 2027 AOI of EUR 2.2bn against consensus of EUR 3.9bn. Rating reiterated; the ADR PO was cut from USD 6.48.

sector_views.rationale: Stellantis is Underperform on weak 2027 volumes, cost inflation and Chinese competition in Europe. Peers Renault and BMW are Neutral and Volkswagen is Buy within the same coverage cluster.

earnings_insights: Q3 2026 (reported): adjusted EBIT EUR 256m, a 0.7% margin, versus Visible Alpha consensus estimate of EUR 162m. Industrial FCF was EUR -4.0bn and inventories rose 14% y/y to 1.4m units.
Q3 2026 regions (reported): North America margin 0.4% and Europe -2.2%. South America (+10.5%) and Middle East & Africa (+14.6%) were resilient.
Q4 2026E (BofA estimate): adjusted EBIT EUR 477m versus Visible Alpha consensus estimate of EUR 532m. Shipments are forecast at -5.6% y/y and diluted EPS at -0.05 versus consensus of 0.03.
FY2026E (BofA estimate): AOI EUR 2,466m versus consensus estimate of EUR 2,582m, and EPS -0.03 versus consensus of 0.00. FY26 results are due in late February 2027.

FY2027E (BofA estimate): AOI EUR 2,184m versus consensus estimate of EUR 3,927m, EPS -0.03 versus consensus of 0.31 in the table, and FCF EUR -2,736m versus consensus of EUR -273m. Revenue is EUR 158.1bn.
FY2028E (BofA estimate): AOI EUR 4,883m versus consensus estimate of EUR 6,506m, EPS 0.66 versus consensus of 1.14, and FCF EUR 667m versus consensus of EUR 1,434m.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Cost inflation and weak volumes absorb VCP savings, leaving the margin well below consensus.
Stellantis is losing US share, and elevated inventory and incentives point to more destocking in Q4.

macro_indicators.reading: c.6.6% vs c.3.9% a year ago
macro_indicators.interpretation: Refinancing costs are rising, which adds to the earnings headwind.

macro_indicators.reading: S&P BBB- negative outlook; Moody's Baa3 stable
macro_indicators.interpretation: Both are one notch above junk. BofA sees meaningful downgrade risk in 2027.

trade_ideas.description: Underperform STLA (EUR 3.50 PO, USD 3.92 ADR PO) on 2027 cash burn and a weaker earnings base
trade_ideas.rationale: BofA expects 2027 AOI c.40% below consensus, a EUR 2.7bn industrial FCF burn and downgrade and dilution overhang until free cash flow turns positive.
trade_ideas.risk: Slower-than-expected raw-material inflation, a stronger USD, a lower oil price supporting V8 demand, and disposals or partnerships for European plants with Chinese OEMs.

risk_factors: Cash burn in 2027 could trigger an S&P or Moody's downgrade to non-investment grade, adding 50-100bp to funding costs.
Capital-raise fears could be an equity overhang, though BofA says a raise is not its base case.
Lower factoring volumes in a downturn, and negative working capital, could accelerate cash erosion.
Raw-material inflation (STLA is not hedged), memory-chip costs, and tariffs weigh on the 2027 margin.
Chinese OEMs taking more share in Europe, and a US recovery too dependent on V8 mix and exposed to fuel prices.
Reporting inconsistencies in the AOI bridge cloud forecasting and underlying earnings visibility.
charts_described: Exhibit 2 compares BofA's 2027E group AOI of EUR 2,184m and industrial FCF of EUR -2,736m with consensus of EUR 3,927m and EUR -273m.
Exhibit 17 states that Stellantis' yield curve is up c150-270bps y/y, with the 10Y at c6.6% versus c3.9%.
Exhibit 22 states that fleet age peaks at 7.8 years in 2028E and falls to 5.3 years by 2030E.
geopolitical: Potential European import restrictions on Chinese OEMs from 2027, and from December per the Q4 discussion, would shape Chinese share gains. PHEV tariffs could push Chinese OEMs back toward BEVs.

Possible higher Canadian import tariffs, a potential EUR -400m burden per BofA, and the end of the IEEPA tariff refund (EUR 400m in H1 26) weigh on North America. Net tariff costs for FY26 are guided at c.EUR 1.0bn.

tension_points.bull_case: Consensus expects 2027 AOI of EUR 3.9bn (2.4% margin) as VCP savings of about EUR 2.0bn and management's targets drive a recovery. Stellantis reiterated positive industrial free cash flow.
tension_points.bear_case: BofA sees EUR 2.2bn AOI (1.4%) because raw-material inflation, tariffs, falling shipments and pricing pressure absorb the savings. A thin launch pipeline and Chinese competition in Europe limit self-help, and industrial FCF is forecast at EUR -2.7bn.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A FY26 results update in late February 2027, with FY27 guidance showing positive industrial FCF and a lower raw-material headwind, would challenge the bear case.
